cues: Readers often sort hardcovers by author before sliding them spine-out onto open tiers.
When titles arrive, someone groups them by genre and leaves gaps for future additions.
Dusting involves lifting rows of novels, wiping each ledge, then returning volumes in order.
A librarian may rearrange reference books by call number across several open levels.
Oversized atlases are laid flat on lower tiers to keep their heavy bindings supported.
New paperbacks are placed upright between bookends so they remain visible and easy to retrieve.
During a move, each row of volumes is removed, packed, and later restored by category.
A child can keep favorite stories within reach by placing them on a low, open tier.
